ai.description: This toad reaches 6–8 cm. It is brown with dark mottling and features prominent, sharp spines across its dorsal surface and head. It is distinguished by its robust build and spiny skin texture.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Scutiger spinosus* is uniquely identified by the presence of prominent, black-tipped conical spines scattered across its dorsal surface, which are absent in other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Scutiger spinosus* inhabits high-altitude alpine meadows and rocky streams in the Eastern Himalayas, typically at elevations between 2,500 and 4,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Spiny Lazy Toad is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates across the forest floor while remaining motionless during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Scutiger spinosus* breeds in mountain streams during the monsoon (June–August). Females deposit small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Spiny Lazy Toad (*Scutiger spinosus*) is endemic to the high-altitude regions of the Eastern Himalayas, specifically occurring in Arunachal Pradesh at elevations above 3,000m.
ai.callDescription: The *Scutiger spinosus* emits a series of short, low-pitched, pulsed croaks while submerged in high-altitude mountain streams.
